v.q: What problem does Spring Cloud Config solve?
o: Centralised, versioned configuration shared by many services
Encrypted traffic between browsers and servers
v.w: Config lives in Git and is served to apps. Secrets still belong in a vault, not in the config repository.

v.q: Which statement about Spring Cloud Config is NOT true?
o: Each service must keep its own copy of the settings
Settings are held in one central place
The store can be a Git repository
v.w: The point of a config server is to avoid per-service copies of the same settings.

v.q: What does service discovery with Eureka or Consul give you?
o: Services look each other up by name, not fixed IPs
Pods are scaled automatically on demand
All services share a single database
One login works across every service
v.w: Instances register on startup and send heartbeats, so callers get only live instances. On Kubernetes you can use built-in DNS instead.

v.q: Which statement about service discovery is NOT true?
v.w: Instances come and go, so callers look up current addresses by name.

v.q: What does Spring Cloud Gateway do?
o: It routes external requests and applies filters such as auth and rate limits
It stores messages for later consumers to read
It generates documentation for every API it fronts
It replicates databases between several regions
v.w: It is a reactive edge service built on WebFlux. Routes match on predicates (path, header) and apply filters.

v.q: Which job should the gateway NOT do?
v.w: It is an edge component. Data belongs to the services.

v.q: Which library is the recommended way to add circuit breakers and retries in Spring Cloud today?
v.w: Hystrix and Ribbon are in maintenance or removed. Resilience4j offers circuit breaker, retry, rate limiter, bulkhead and time limiter.

v.q: Which library is deprecated for circuit breaking in Spring Cloud?
v.w: Hystrix is in maintenance mode. Resilience4j is the current choice.

v.q: A declarative HTTP client for calling another service by interface is provided by:
o: OpenFeign or the Spring `RestClient` with HTTP interfaces
Spring Batch with a job and step configuration
v.w: You write an interface with annotated methods and Spring generates the implementation, with timeouts and resilience added through configuration.

v.q: Which tool lets you declare an HTTP client as a Java interface?
v.w: Annotated methods describe the call, and Spring generates the implementation.

v.q: A client calls a service with a 30-second default timeout while the service is hanging. What is the best protection?
o: Set short explicit timeouts and add a circuit breaker with a fallback
Retry immediately and without any upper limit on tries
Raise the timeout to five minutes so the call can finish
Give the caller many more threads to wait with
v.w: Every remote call needs a timeout. Without one, slow dependencies tie up threads and cascade failures upwards.

v.q: Which setting is NOT a good protection against a hanging dependency?
v.w: Long timeouts keep threads busy, so the caller runs out of capacity.

v.q: How does a distributed trace id help in a microservices system?
o: It links logs and spans of one request across every service
It authenticates the user inside each service
v.w: Propagated in headers (W3C `traceparent`), it lets you follow one request end to end in Zipkin, Tempo or Jaeger.

v.q: Which value shows one request flowing through three services?
v.w: The same trace id appears in every span and, with correlation, in the logs.

v.q: Why is client-side load balancing common with service discovery?
o: The caller picks an instance from the registry, saving a hop
It removes the need for any service instances to exist
It encrypts every single call automatically for you
It stores the results of each call in a local cache
v.w: Spring Cloud LoadBalancer picks among registered instances. On Kubernetes the Service object does similar work server-side.

v.q: Which statement about client-side load balancing is NOT true?
o: It needs an extra proxy hop
v.w: The caller talks to the chosen instance directly, so there is no extra hop.
